columns.name: dedup_key
columns.semantic_note: internal only, not meaningful to read directly

columns.name: timestamp_begin
columns.semantic_note: operation/trade date; equals timestamp_end when the source doesn't distinguish it from the value/settlement date

columns.name: timestamp_end
columns.semantic_note: canonical timestamp — value/settlement date when the source distinguishes it (meinElba, Sella), else equal to timestamp_begin. Can precede timestamp_begin: a retroactive value date is real bank behavior, not a parsing error.

columns.name: domain
columns.semantic_note: 'bank' (meinElba, Sella) or 'investment' (Trade Republic cash+trades) — only ever these 2 values. This is NOT a merchant or company name: 'Amazon', 'PayPal', etc. never appear here, they are in the merchant column instead.

columns.name: institution
columns.semantic_note: human-readable institution name — exactly one of these 3 literal values: 'meinElba (Raiffeisen)', 'Banca Sella', 'Trade Republic'. Not 'Sella' alone, not 'Raiffeisen' alone — use the full string or LIKE '%Sella%' / LIKE '%Trade Republic%'.

columns.name: amount
columns.semantic_note: signed: positive=income, negative=expense. Native currency, never auto-converted.

columns.name: transaction_type
columns.semantic_note: income/expense/transfer/investment/interest/tax/cash_deposit/cash_withdrawal/fee/unknown. For Trade Republic, both BUY and SELL rows have transaction_type='investment' — 'buy'/'sell' are never values of this column. To tell a purchase from a sale, use category_raw (LIKE '%/ BUY' or '%/ SELL') or the sign of shares (positive=buy, negative=sell).

columns.name: category
columns.semantic_note: from our shared taxonomy — 'unknown' whenever the source gives no explicit native signal (never guessed from generic keywords)

columns.name: category_raw
columns.semantic_note: original native category/type string, always preserved even when category is 'unknown'. For Trade Republic rows this is 'NATIVE_CATEGORY / NATIVE_TYPE' (e.g. 'TRADING / BUY' vs 'TRADING / SELL') — the only place a buy is distinguishable from a sell, since transaction_type and category both collapse to 'investment' for both (see TRADE_REPUBLIC_TYPE_MAP in money_ingest.py). To find purchases only: category_raw LIKE '%/ BUY' or shares > 0; sales: '%/ SELL' or shares < 0.

columns.name: merchant
columns.semantic_note: normalized merchant name from a small curated list — most real merchants stay unmatched (None) on purpose, see module docstring. Trade Republic is never a value here (it's an institution, not a merchant) — use the institution column for it.

columns.name: description_full
columns.semantic_note: free-text description; any 'IBAN: <value>' substring is redacted (see module docstring's privacy note) — ISIN codes in the same text are NOT touched

columns.name: isin
columns.semantic_note: security identifier, when this transaction relates to one (native field for Trade Republic trades, extracted from free text for others when present)

columns.name: instrument_name
columns.semantic_note: native Trade Republic instrument name string, exactly as the broker wrote it (e.g. a company's official listed name, not a translated or colloquial phrase like 'azioni NVIDIA'). Match it with LIKE '%keyword%' or run a discovery query (SELECT DISTINCT instrument_name FROM transactions WHERE instrument_name LIKE '%...%') first — never an exact string you guessed. isin is a more reliable filter when you already know the ISIN.

columns.name: shares
columns.semantic_note: signed quantity, populated only for Trade Republic BUY/SELL rows. Sign is a reliable buy/sell signal in the real data: positive=buy, negative=sell (amount sign runs the other way: negative=buy/cash-out, positive=sell/cash-in) — see category_raw for the same distinction via the native type string

columns.name: original_amount
columns.semantic_note: amount in original_currency before FX conversion, when the source reports one

columns.name: native_id
columns.semantic_note: native transaction id when the source provides one (Trade Republic transaction_id, Sella Codice identificativo); None for meinElba/generic

columns.name: is_unusual
columns.semantic_note: native boolean, 0/1 — z-score flag within (category, currency, domain), see ANOMALY_* config; 0 when the group is too small to judge (< 5 comparable transactions)
